summary: Independent review of the task 21.10 deliverable docs/implementation/21.10/security-review.json (the release security review of the corrected candidate, produced by the security-reviewer). The gate requirement is met and I confirmed it independently rather than accepting the report's own tally. (1) Coherence/completeness: the report carries every required field - task, attempt, reviewer, reviewer_status (PASS_WITH_FINDINGS, a value in the docs/agent-contracts.md security-reviewer enum), open_blocker_high, artifact, sec_21_5_01_disposition, 12 findings each with id/severity/status/area/summary/evidence/recommended_action, open_blocker_high_detail, secret/auth/state/input path inventories, reproductions, prior_findings_reconciled (16 entries), limitations (6), summary, ready_for_next_task, and user_decision_required. Severity and status tokens conform to the contract enums; scripts/check-agents.sh reports 'status/severity tokens conform' and PASS. (2) Gate: the report has zero findings at severity BLOCKER or HIGH, and its own detail block (blocker 0, high 0, open_medium 0, open_low 3, informational_noted 8, resolved_this_pass 1) matches the 12 findings it actually lists (1 MEDIUM resolved, 3 LOW open, 8 INFORMATIONAL noted), so open_blocker_high = 0 is the true count and not an undercount. SEC-21.5-01 has an explicit, reasoned disposition in a dedicated sec_21_5_01_disposition field and a matching prior_findings_reconciled entry, not merely a status flip. (3) Independent reproduction against the SHIPPED binary, not the source: I extracted artifacts/ArrTags_1.2.0.0.zip to a reviewer-owned temp directory, confirmed its identity (619,636 bytes, SHA-256 3e59cb06..., MD5 f3b50a91..., 7 entries, per-entry SHA-256 equal to the docs/release/build-and-release.md table), and confirmed the packaged ArrTags.dll (eae2cbab...b235d) is byte-identical to a Release build of the audited source. Against that extracted assembly I wrote my own two-origin loopback probe: reflection over the two private handler factories and the resolved HttpClientFactoryOptions of all four named clients shows AllowAutoRedirect=False on every one (strict keeps strict cert validation, both .Insecure keep DangerousAcceptAnyServerCertificateValidator); the shipped registration produces 1 request to the configured origin, 0 requests to the 3xx Location origin, no key egress, and a 93-character InvalidResponse/Never error whose message contains no key, no body sentinel, and no Location value. My pre-fix control (the same shipped SonarrClient + SecretLease code against a bare AddHttpClient registration, i.e. the exact 21.5 shape) does deliver the key to the second origin (1 request, key present), so the harness discriminates and the negative is a real fix. That is a third independent reproduction of the resolution beyond the report's own. I also confirmed ClassifyStatus consults the new '>= 300 and < 400' arm before ReadContentAsync in both clients, and that these are the only two HttpRequestMessage construction sites (GET only, no body). (4) Carried and new findings: SEC-21.5-02/03/04 are carried at the same LOW severity with status open and each is re-verified with a reproduction, not dropped; I independently reproduced 02 and 03 against the shipped assembly (Cf U+202E/U+200B/U+2066/U+2069 and Zl/Zp U+2028/U+2029 pass verbatim while Cc U+0001 is stripped; a Windows path and a UNC path are emitted whole at 32 and 34 scalars; POSIX controls pass; a 300-scalar name truncates to 128; whitespace-only falls back to the item id). The two new INFORMATIONAL findings are both accurate, including SEC-21.10-01's contested claim: I unwrapped a real factory-created client on this runtime and the .NET 10 IHttpClientFactory default primary handler is System.Net.Http.SocketsHttpHandler with AllowAutoRedirect=True, not HttpClientHandler, so the 21.7 worker report's stated basis ('the .NET client factory's default primary handler is HttpClientHandler') is indeed factually wrong while the registrator's code and conclusion are right. SEC-21.10-02 is confirmed too: the manifest.json 1.2.0.0 changelog one-liner contains no mention of the redirect behaviour change, while docs/changelog/v1.2.0.md, docs/architecture/07 and /11, and the ADR-005 implementation note all do. (5) Scope discipline: the only change in the working tree for this task is the untracked docs/implementation/21.10/ directory; git diff e172c4c HEAD -- src/ArrTags touches only the registrator's HTTP client registration, the two ClassifyStatus switches, and the new test file, so the review changed no product code, test, canonical document, PLANS.md, state.json, manifest.json, or artifact, and created no commit or tag. I re-ran the default suite (Failed 0, Passed 1,937, Skipped 66, Total 2,003) and the host-guarded suite against the pinned Jellyfin 12.0.0 host (Failed 0, Passed 1,957, Skipped 46, Total 2,003) and the focused ProviderRedirectTransportTests (Failed 0, Passed 10), all equal to the figures the report and docs/release/build-and-release.md record; scripts/check-docs.sh and scripts/check-agents.sh both PASS. Two observations are recorded as `noted` rather than as required changes: the report's SEC-21.10-01 property-by-property equivalence listing omits two real (non-security) differences between the factory default SocketsHttpHandler and the HttpClientHandler the fix installs - PooledConnectionLifetime (factory default 2 minutes vs the fix's infinite) and ClientCertificateOptions/LocalCertificateSelectionCallback - which are worth recording but change no security-relevant property and do not affect any conclusion; and the mandatory state.json reports entry for task 21.10 is still to be added by the orchestrator at commit time, exactly the contract-defined interim state the 21.7 reviewer recorded.

findings.summary: SEC-21.10-01's property-by-property equivalence list omits two real non-security differences between the factory default SocketsHttpHandler and the installed HttpClientHandler; the finding's conclusion is unaffected.
findings.detail: SEC-21.10-01 asserts the effective transport configuration is 'identical to the factory default in every security-relevant property' and enumerates the properties it compared. My independent full property dump of a factory-created client versus the registrator's CreateStrictHandler output (both unwrapped to System.Net.Http.SocketsHttpHandler) shows the enumerated security-relevant properties are indeed identical, and that AllowAutoRedirect is the only security-relevant difference, so the finding's substance is correct. The enumeration is not exhaustive, though: PooledConnectionLifetime is 2 minutes on the factory default and infinite on the installed handler, and ClientCertificateOptions is Automatic on the default while the HttpClientHandler surface reports Manual with a non-null SslOptions.LocalCertificateSelectionCallback. Neither is security-relevant for this integration (no client certificate is ever presented and no connection is deliberately kept alive for a security reason), so the finding's conclusion and the 'noted' status stand, and no gate item depends on the enumeration being complete. Recorded so a future reader does not treat the listing as an exhaustive equivalence proof.
evidence: My property dump (/tmp/21.10/probe4) of the factory default versus CreateStrictHandler, both unwrapped to SocketsHttpHandler: DIFF AllowAutoRedirect True/False, DIFF ClientCertificateOptions Automatic/Manual, DIFF PooledConnectionLifetime 00:02:00/-00:00:00.0010000, DIFF SSL.LocalCertificateSelectionCallback null/<delegate>; no other difference in any enumerated or unenumerated property
docs/implementation/21.10/security-review.json SEC-21.10-01 evidence: 'SslOptions/connection-property dumps identical line for line apart from the redirect flag'
src/ArrTags/PluginLifecycle/ArrTagsServiceRegistrator.cs:241-247 CreateStrictHandler sets only AllowAutoRedirect = false, so neither property is set by the plugin
findings.recommended_action: No change required for this task. If a later task amends or supersedes SEC-21.10-01, add PooledConnectionLifetime and the client-certificate surface to the enumerated differences so the record is not read as an exhaustive equivalence.
